title: Polynomial exact metric sparsifiers with a crossing-edge budget
formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(C,c>0\) such that the following holds? For every finite simple undirected unweighted graph \(G=(V,E)\), terminal set \(T\subseteq V\) of size r, and integer \(p\ge 0\), there is a set \(Z\subseteq E\) with |\(Z|\le C(1+p+r)^{c}\) having this universal property: for every finite nonempty label set D, every metric \(\mu :D\times D\to R_{\ge 0}\), and every terminal labeling \(\tau :T\to D\), if there exists a labeling \(\lambda :V\to D\) extending \(\tau\) with at most p crossing edges, then some labeling \(\lambda\)* of minimum \(\mu\)-cost among all such budget-feasible extensions has all its crossing edges in Z. The same Z must work simultaneously for every \(D,\mu ,\tau\) and depends only on G,T,p. This is the polynomial-size version of the contraction-based metric-sparsifier property in the source’s Theorem 22; that theorem’s earlier quasipolynomial upper-bound claim was later retracted.
context:
A 0-Extension instance extends fixed labels on terminals to the rest of a graph while minimizing metric distances across edges. The desired sparsifier is chosen before either the metric or the terminal labels, and must retain an optimal extension whenever the crossing-edge budget is feasible.

Theorem 22 uses \(p+r\), with p counting disagreeing endpoints and r counting terminals. This differs from the total terminal degree used for ordinary multicut-mimicking networks elsewhere in the paper. An unrestricted terminal-count lower bound is therefore not automatically a lower bound for this question.

The corrected March 2021 version explicitly reports an incorrect proof for the preliminary 0-Extension claims and retracts the claimed quasipolynomial metric sparsifiers. It retains the underlying existence question. The retraction also appears in the accepted journal manuscript; the paper’s ordinary multicut results and the earlier Reidl–Wahlström results are stated to be unaffected.

Anand, Lee, Li and Saranurak’s 2024 work obtains randomized polynomial-time ordinary multicut-mimicking networks with \(k^{O(\log ^{2} k)}\) size, where k is total terminal degree. Their preserved quantities are minimum multiway-cut cardinalities for terminal partitions. This does not reestablish the retracted all-metrics, crossing-budget property.
why: Would determine whether a graph can be compressed once for every metric-labeling objective under a bounded number of label changes, a stronger form of reusable exact information than preserving ordinary terminal cut values.
status_note: Recovered the exact universal-set property from conference Theorem 22 and read the corrected full version’s explicit retraction and retained question. Checked the journal metadata and indexed author-manuscript retraction, the 2024 multicut theorem and later sparsifier searches through 12 September 2026. No resolution of this exact metric/budget property was found; the retracted theorem is not treated as established progress.

sentences: A graph with terminals is queried by choosing labels for the terminals and a metric on the labels.
The goal is a small retained edge set that supports an optimal extension for every such query.
Only labelings with at most p crossing edges are compared, and the retained set must have size polynomial in p plus the number of terminals.
The original claimed quasipolynomial metric-sparsifier result was explicitly retracted in the corrected paper.
Ordinary multicut sparsifiers preserve a different collection of values and do not settle this universal metric question.

definitions: A crossing edge of \(\lambda\) is an edge uv with \(\lambda (u)\ne \lambda (v)\). Write \(X(\lambda )=\{uv\in E:\lambda (u)\ne \lambda (v)\}\) and \(\operatorname{cost}_{\mu}(\lambda )=\sum_{uv\in E}\mu (\lambda (u),\lambda (v))\). A metric has \(\mu (a,b)=\mu (b,a), \mu (a,b)=0\) exactly when \(a=b\), and \(\mu (a,c)\le \mu (a,b)+\mu (b,c)\). The admissible labelings for a query are \(B(G,T,p,D,\tau )\)={\(\lambda :V\to D:\lambda |_{T}=\tau\) and |\(X(\lambda )|\le p\)}. If B is nonempty, the finite set \(D^{V}\) ensures that \(\min _{\lambda \in B}\operatorname{cost}_{\mu}(\lambda )\) is attained. The universal requirement is that this minimum equals the minimum with the additional constraint \(X(\lambda )\subseteq Z\); in particular the latter feasible set must be nonempty. The number p bounds crossings, not the real-valued metric cost. Labeling \(\tau\) need not be injective or surjective, and |D| is unbounded independently of \(p+r\). The constants C,c may not depend on the graph, budget, label set, metric or terminal labeling. Using \(1+p+r\) only handles zero parameters and is asymptotically equivalent to polynomial size in \(p+r\). Restricting all edges outside Z to have equal endpoint labels is exactly the labeling constraint imposed by contracting those edges; Z measures the original retained edges. The question is existence of this universal set, not the running time to find it, so it neither assumes rational metric entries nor a numerical oracle for them. Exact equality of optimum values is required; no multiplicative or additive error is allowed.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated universal polynomial bound, or refute it by showing that no fixed constants C,c can bound the required retained edges over all G,T,p. A negative result must respect the quantifier order: every candidate small Z must fail for some label set, metric and terminal labeling with a feasible budgeted extension. Hardness of finding a small Z does not disprove its existence. Bounds for one fixed metric, a fixed number of labels, ordinary terminal cut values, or approximate values do not settle this target.
